headline: Make an extraordinary journey easier to choose.
intro: Galápagos travel is a considered purchase. The work connects inspiring destination creative with clear landing pages, qualified inquiries, and a better view of what happens after the click.
purpose: Helping travelers discover remarkable places through a journey they can understand and plan with confidence.
role: Paid media strategy, campaign optimization, landing-page development and testing, and collaboration on inquiry-to-sale measurement across GalapagosIsland.net and LuxuryCruisesGalapagos.com.
challenge: Beautiful imagery can attract attention. Turning that interest into a qualified travel inquiry also requires a clear offer, useful vessel and itinerary information, and a reliable handoff to the sales team.
decision: Connect the creative promise to a practical inquiry journey—and evaluate forms alongside the sales pipeline.
work: Clarify the journey
Develop and compare landing-page experiences around destination discovery, vessel choices, reassurance, and an obvious inquiry step.
Coordinate the channels
Work across Google Search, Performance Max, and Meta, with different roles for high-intent discovery and visual storytelling.
Follow the lead
Review form submissions, session URLs, won opportunities, and conversion values to connect campaign decisions to commercial context.
metrics: September 2026 · agenda snapshot across the two travel sites
Form submissions associated with the landing page
Cumulative figure recorded October 12, 2026; page-specific reporting
measurement: Figures are reported in the October 12, 2026 working agenda. The 142 submissions and September won value cover different scopes and periods and should not be combined into a conversion or ROAS claim. Website migration and attribution reconciliation were ongoing.
learning: A page can generate interest without telling the whole commercial story. Reviewing the inquiry path and sales feedback together gives the team a more useful basis for the next test.
previewCaption: Selected Galápagos Island landing-page work. Preserved campaign example.
mediaCaption: Saved Google placement preview showing how the travel story appears in context.

headline: Let the whole experience tell the story.
intro: A premium cruise is more than a vessel. Suites, wildlife, itineraries, service, and the feeling of being there all have a role in helping the right traveler take the next step.
purpose: Bringing exceptional Galápagos experiences within reach of travelers looking for a meaningful, carefully considered journey.
role: Google and Meta campaign strategy and optimization, collaborative creative development, landing-page CRO, and inquiry-path testing.
challenge: The campaign needs to express a high-value experience while making choices and next steps feel simple. More images alone do not resolve questions about which itinerary fits or what happens after an inquiry.
decision: Use the richness of the brand’s own footage, then simplify the path from inspiration to a conversation.
work: Show the experience
Bring vessel interiors, ocean views, and destination footage into flexible-media campaigns and placement-aware creative.
Test the inquiry path
Compare landing-page approaches and form-versus-call experiences, reviewing whether the visitor understands the next step.
Roll out carefully
Introduce a preferred landing-page variation in stages and monitor campaign performance instead of changing every variable at once.
metrics: September 2026 · reported in the same agenda
measurement: The October 20, 2026 working agenda reports these Meta cost-per-form figures. October is a partial month, so this is a directional comparison, not a controlled test or a claim of incremental revenue. Revenue totals shared with La Selva are intentionally excluded.
learning: Premium creative and disciplined testing work together. A strong visual story still benefits from simpler page flow, clearer choices, and a measured rollout.
previewCaption: Selected landing-page experience for Golden Galápagos Cruises.
mediaCaption: Saved Instagram placement preview. Brand footage and campaign support are collaborative work.

headline: Help the right people see a path to renewal.
intro: Retreat marketing connects a personal intention with an experience people can understand and choose. The work spans audience-led messaging, paid media, landing-page experiments, and the practical path from interest to booking.
purpose: Helping people discover opportunities to pause, learn, and invest in their wellbeing.
role: Paid media strategy and optimization, collaborative ad-copy and creative direction, landing-page concepts and technical feedback, experiment planning, and funnel analysis alongside the retreat team.
challenge: Different programs speak to different needs. The experience must make the offer and next step clear, while measurement distinguishes campaign performance from the booking and consultation process.
decision: Work on the whole journey: audience, message, page, measurement, and the next human interaction.
work: Understand the audience
Develop message angles and creative around the needs behind Panchakarma, Rest & Relaxation, and other retreat programs.
Make the offer tangible
Create and review landing-page variations, webinar-funnel concepts, and copy and layout recommendations with the client’s team.
Learn across the funnel
Plan controlled page tests and review campaign reporting alongside consultation and booking behavior. Separate a promising hypothesis from an established result.
metrics: Same R&R metric as described in the October 15 agenda
measurement: The October 15, 2026 working agenda distinguishes Google Ads conversion ROAS from broader sales reporting. These values refer to the specified R&R metric only, not the whole retreat center or a controlled attribution study. Proposed page tests are described as planned work, not completed wins.
learning: A campaign’s next opportunity may be the message, the page, or the booking journey. Reviewing those together creates better questions than treating ad performance in isolation.
previewCaption: Selected Panchakarma opt-in concept. A creative and landing-page example, not a performance result.
mediaCaption: Preserved Panchakarma campaign preview. Production and strategy involve multiple collaborators.

headline: From first click to first class.
intro: For a parent, gymnastics can mean more confidence, new friendships, and a place for their child’s energy. Across locations, the marketing needs to make that possibility clear—and make the next step easy.
purpose: Helping more families discover spaces where children can move, build skills, and find confidence.
role: Multi-location Google and Meta campaign management, seasonal and free-trial creative, landing-page messaging and testing, and funnel-reporting collaboration.
challenge: Each gym has its own identity, programs, and local audience. Seasonal camp demand and year-round trials also require different messages, while the business needs to distinguish a lead from a booked, attended, and converted trial.
decision: Keep the local personality. Build a more consistent system for creative, testing, and the path to enrollment.
work: Speak to parents
Explore confidence, belonging, skill development, and convenience as distinct message angles rather than treating every family as the same audience.
Build across locations
Develop seasonal camp and trial campaigns with brand-specific creative, including Scottsdale and Capital Round Rock examples.
Measure the next step
Review trial attendance and conversion, campaign KPI definitions, and the feasibility of faster landing-page variations before expanding tests.
metrics: Comparison noted in the same September reporting
measurement: Figures come from the September 2026 entries in the Powers weekly agenda. They describe reported trial conversion, not ad-click conversion or a randomized test. Location mix, seasonality, follow-up, and KPI definitions matter. They are not presented as results caused solely by advertising.
learning: Growth is more useful when the team can explain what is growing. Lead volume, trial attendance, and enrollment each answer a different question.
previewCaption: Scottsdale back-to-school free-trial creative approved for this portfolio.
mediaCaption: Capital Round Rock camp carousel example, preserving the gym’s own visual identity.
